---
title: "Fit synthetic patients"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
---

Fits a few synthetic patients from `python/genertate_synth_AT_trial_data.ipynb` with `stan/model_switchable.stan` and
checks the fits: sampler diagnostics, trace and pairs plots, recovery of the true parameters, posterior predictive
checks and LOO.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, cmdstanr, posterior, bayesplot, loo, here, patchwork, knitr)
source(here("R/functions.R"))
source(here("R/synth_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw())
```

## Settings

Fits are saved in `<fit_dir>/<window>` and reused on the next run, unless `refit` is TRUE.

```{r run-settings}
patients      <- c(3, 4, 6)
window        <- "two_cycles" #first_cycle, two_cycles or full_history (synth_windows in R/synth_functions.R)
chains        <- 4
iter_warmup   <- 1000
iter_sampling <- 1000
adapt_delta   <- 0.95
refit         <- FALSE
synth_dir     <- here("synth_data")
fit_dir       <- here("fits/synth_rmd")
```

The priors are `priorDic` from the notebook, which the patients were drawn from. scipy `lognorm(s, scale)` is
`lognormal(log(scale), s)`. K is fixed at 1, as when the patients were generated, so `K_prior` is not used.
`rFrac` is beta(1, 20) as in the notebook, not beta(0.3, 40) as in `R/fit_synth_switchable.R` (BUGS.md D2).

```{r settings}
priors <- list(
  cost_prior     = c(1, 1),
  turnover_prior = c(1.2, 2.5),
  n0_prior       = c(2, 2),
  rFrac_prior    = c(1, 20),
  K_prior        = c(log(2), 0.8),
  rS_prior       = c(log(0.012), 0.6),
  dD_prior       = c(log(2.5), 0.6),
  sigma_prior    = c(-5, 1)
)
fixed_vals <- list(K = 1)
fit_params <- c("cost", "turnover", "n0", "rFrac", "rS", "dD", "sigma")

n_cycles <- synth_windows[[window]]
out_dir  <- file.path(fit_dir, window)
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

#true parameters, renamed to match the Stan model
truth <- list.files(synth_dir, pattern = "^randSynthetic\\d+Patients\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE) |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "unique_quiet") |>
  select(patient = PatientId, cost, turnover, n0, rFrac, rS, dD, sigma) |>
  filter(patient %in% patients)
kable(truth, digits = 3)
```

## Data

The line is the true size relative to the initial size, on the same scale as the observations. Points are the noisy
observations. Filled points are the ones in the fitting window. Shaded stretches are on treatment.

```{r data, fig.height = 2.5 * length(patients)}
trajectories <- map_dfr(patients, \(id) load_synth_trajectory(id, synth_dir) |> mutate(patient = id))
visits <- map_dfr(patients, \(id) load_synth_patient(id, synth_dir) |> mutate(patient = id)) |>
  mutate(in_window = CycleId <= n_cycles)

#runs of constant dose on the daily grid, as rectangles. A run ends where the next one starts
treated <- trajectories |>
  group_by(patient, run = consecutive_id(DrugConcentration)) |>
  summarise(start = first(Time), dose = first(DrugConcentration), .groups = "drop_last") |>
  mutate(end = lead(start, default = Inf)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(dose > 0)

ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = treated, aes(xmin = start, xmax = pmin(end, max(trajectories$Time)), ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = "grey85") +
  geom_line(data = trajectories, aes(Time, TumourSizeNorm)) +
  geom_point(data = visits, aes(Time, PSA, shape = in_window), size = 1.5) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 1), name = "In window") +
  facet_wrap(~patient, ncol = 1, scales = "free", labeller = label_both) +
  labs(y = "size / initial size")
```

## Fit

The Stan data come from `make_switchable_stan_data` in `R/synth_functions.R`, as in `R/fit_synth_switchable.R`: n0 is
fitted, and the model is compared with the observations directly (`mu = (S + R) / n0` in Stan).
`tests/test_stan_matches_simulator.R` checks that with the true parameters, Stan's `mu` equals the simulated trajectory.

```{r inits}
#one draw from the prior per chain. Stan's default inits (uniform(-2, 2) on the unconstrained scale) put e.g. rS up to 7,
#where the ODE gets stiff and chains got stuck in warmup
draw_prior_init <- function() {
  list(cost_free     = array(rbeta(1, priors$cost_prior[1], priors$cost_prior[2])),
       turnover_free = array(rbeta(1, priors$turnover_prior[1], priors$turnover_prior[2])),
       n0_free       = array(rbeta(1, priors$n0_prior[1], priors$n0_prior[2])),
       #small rFrac draws can underflow to 0, which is outside the support
       rFrac_free    = array(max(rbeta(1, priors$rFrac_prior[1], priors$rFrac_prior[2]), 1e-8)),
       rS_free       = array(rlnorm(1, priors$rS_prior[1], priors$rS_prior[2])),
       dD_free       = array(rlnorm(1, priors$dD_prior[1], priors$dD_prior[2])),
       sigma         = rlnorm(1, priors$sigma_prior[1], priors$sigma_prior[2]))
}
```

A fit that gets stuck in a stiff region of the ODE can run for a long time. For many patients, use
`R/fit_synth_switchable.R`, which runs each fit with a time limit.

```{r fit, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
stan_model <- cmdstan_model(here("stan/model_switchable.stan"))

fit_one <- function(patient_id) {
  fit_path <- make_fit_path(patient_id, dir = out_dir)
  if (file.exists(fit_path) && !refit) return(readRDS(fit_path))
  set.seed(patient_id) #inits are seeded per patient
  start <- Sys.time()
  fit <- stan_model$sample(data            = make_switchable_stan_data(patient_id, n_cycles, priors, fixed_vals,
                                                                   dir = synth_dir),
                           init            = map(seq_len(chains), \(i) draw_prior_init()),
                           chains          = chains,
                           parallel_chains = chains,
                           iter_warmup     = iter_warmup,
                           iter_sampling   = iter_sampling,
                           adapt_delta     = adapt_delta,
                           seed            = patient_id,
                           refresh         = 0,
                           show_messages   = FALSE)
  fit$save_object(fit_path)
  #run time and settings next to the fit, as in fit_synth_patients. Fit objects are locked, so they can't hold them
  saveRDS(list(seconds = as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start, units = "secs")), priors = priors,
               fixed_vals = fixed_vals, n_cycles = n_cycles, adapt_delta = adapt_delta),
          sub("\\.rds$", "_settings.rds", fit_path))
  fit
}

fits <- set_names(patients) |> map(fit_one)
```

## Sampler diagnostics

What to look for: no divergences, no hits of the maximum tree depth, E-BFMI above 0.3, R-hat below 1.01 and bulk and
tail ESS above about 400 for every parameter.

```{r diagnostics}
diagnostics <- imap_dfr(fits, \(fit, id) {
  sampler <- fit$diagnostic_summary(quiet = TRUE)
  summ    <- fit$summary(fit_params, "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail")
  tibble(patient      = as.integer(id),
         n_obs        = fit$metadata()$stan_variable_sizes$PSA_pred,
         seconds      = readRDS(sub("\\.rds$", "_settings.rds", make_fit_path(as.integer(id), out_dir)))$seconds,
         divergences  = sum(sampler$num_divergent),
         treedepth    = sum(sampler$num_max_treedepth),
         min_ebfmi    = min(sampler$ebfmi),
         max_rhat     = max(summ$rhat, na.rm = TRUE),
         min_ess_bulk = min(summ$ess_bulk, na.rm = TRUE),
         min_ess_tail = min(summ$ess_tail, na.rm = TRUE))
})
kable(diagnostics, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 3, 0, 0))
```

Per-parameter summaries:

```{r summaries}
imap_dfr(fits, \(fit, id) fit$summary(fit_params, "median", ~quantile(.x, c(0.05, 0.95)), "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail") |>
           mutate(patient = as.integer(id), .before = 1)) |>
  kable(digits = 3)
```

### Trace plots

Chains should overlap and look like noise around a stable level.

```{r trace, fig.height = 6}
color_scheme_set("mix-blue-red")
iwalk(fits, \(fit, id) print(mcmc_trace(fit$draws(fit_params), facet_args = list(ncol = 4)) + ggtitle(paste("patient", id))))
```

### Pairs plots

Strong correlations or banana shapes show parameters the data can't separate. Divergent transitions are shown in red,
and if they cluster in one region, that is where the sampler has trouble.

```{r pairs, fig.height = 8, fig.width = 8}
pair_params <- c("cost", "turnover", "n0", "rS", "dD")
iwalk(fits, \(fit, id) {
  print(mcmc_pairs(fit$draws(pair_params), np = nuts_params(fit), off_diag_fun = "hex",
                   np_style = pairs_style_np(div_color = "red")))
  cat("patient", id, "\n")
})
```

## Parameter recovery

Posterior median with 50% and 90% intervals for each patient, against the true value (red cross). The grey band is the
prior's 90% interval. A posterior that fills the grey band means the data say little about that parameter.

```{r recovery, fig.height = 5, fig.width = 10}
posterior_intervals <- imap_dfr(fits, \(fit, id) {
  fit$draws(fit_params, format = "draws_df") |>
    as_tibble() |>
    select(all_of(fit_params)) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "param") |>
    group_by(param) |>
    summarise(median = median(value),
              q05 = quantile(value, .05), q25 = quantile(value, .25),
              q75 = quantile(value, .75), q95 = quantile(value, .95)) |>
    mutate(patient = as.integer(id))
})

true_values <- truth |> pivot_longer(-patient, names_to = "param", values_to = "truth")

#90% prior intervals. Beta priors are given as shape parameters, lognormal priors as log-scale mean and sd
prior_intervals <- tibble(param = fit_params) |>
  mutate(prior = map(param, \(p) priors[[paste0(p, "_prior")]]),
         is_beta = param %in% c("cost", "turnover", "n0", "rFrac"),
         lo = map2_dbl(prior, is_beta, \(pr, b) if (b) qbeta(.05, pr[1], pr[2]) else qlnorm(.05, pr[1], pr[2])),
         hi = map2_dbl(prior, is_beta, \(pr, b) if (b) qbeta(.95, pr[1], pr[2]) else qlnorm(.95, pr[1], pr[2])))

posterior_intervals |>
  left_join(true_values, by = c("patient", "param")) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = factor(patient))) +
  geom_rect(data = prior_intervals, aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            fill = "grey90") +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = q05, xmax = q95)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = q25, xmax = q75), linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_point(aes(x = median), size = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(x = truth), shape = 4, colour = "red", size = 3, stroke = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~param, scales = "free_x", nrow = 2) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "patient")
```

## Posterior predictive check

The ribbons are 50% and 90% intervals of `PSA_pred`, a new noisy measurement at each fitted visit. Points are the
observations, the line is the true trajectory. About 90% of points should fall inside the outer ribbon.

```{r ppc, fig.height = 2.5 * length(patients)}
ppc <- imap_dfr(fits, \(fit, id) {
  obs <- visits |> filter(patient == as.integer(id), in_window)
  fit$draws("PSA_pred", format = "draws_matrix") |>
    as_tibble() |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "i") |>
    mutate(i = parse_number(i)) |>
    group_by(i) |>
    summarise(q05 = quantile(value, .05), q25 = quantile(value, .25),
              q75 = quantile(value, .75), q95 = quantile(value, .95)) |>
    mutate(Time = obs$Time[i], PSA = obs$PSA[i], patient = as.integer(id))
})

ppc |> group_by(patient) |> summarise(coverage_90 = mean(PSA >= q05 & PSA <= q95)) |> kable(digits = 2)

#the true trajectory up to the last fitted visit
fitted_trajectories <- trajectories |>
  inner_join(ppc |> group_by(patient) |> summarise(end = max(Time)), by = "patient") |>
  filter(Time <= end)

ggplot(ppc, aes(Time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = .25) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75), fill = "steelblue", alpha = .4) +
  geom_line(data = fitted_trajectories, aes(y = TumourSizeNorm)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = PSA), size = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~patient, ncol = 1, scales = "free", labeller = label_both) +
  labs(y = "size / initial size")
```

## LOO

PSIS-LOO from `log_lik`. Pareto k above 0.7 marks visits that the fit depends on strongly, so the LOO estimate for
that patient is unreliable.

```{r loo, warning = FALSE}
imap_dfr(fits, \(fit, id) {
  l <- fit$loo()
  tibble(patient  = as.integer(id),
         elpd_loo = l$estimates["elpd_loo", "Estimate"],
         se       = l$estimates["elpd_loo", "SE"],
         p_loo    = l$estimates["p_loo", "Estimate"],
         n_k_over_0.7 = sum(pareto_k_values(l) > 0.7))
}) |>
  kable(digits = 2)
```
